To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BMAA causes membrane depolarization, calcium accumulation, and cell shrinkage in DAergic neurons through activation of mGluR-1 receptors, TRP channels, and to some extent AMPA receptors.

BMAA causes electrophysiological alterations and calcium overload in substantia nigra dopaminergic (DAergic) neurons by activating metabotropic glutamate receptors, transient receptor potential channels, and to some extent AMPA receptors.
(i) BMAA is an mGluR agonist, (ii) mGluRs are expressed in SNpc DAergic neurons and (iii) mGluR activation causes calcium influx and cyt-c release.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms involved in the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's Disease (PD).
the study of the molecular mechanism by which the neurotoxin BMAA induces the electrophysioligcal and toxic actions in the dopaminergic neurons of substantia nigra.
the mechanisms of BMAA-induced neuronal toxicity, with a particular focus on the role of glutamate receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BMAA, acting on mGluR-activated pathways, is the most likely culprit for the parkinsonian features in ALS-PDC and possibly also in idiopathic PD.
BMAA is not the cause of PD, but it is a potential contributing factor to PD.
BMAA, a neurotoxin found in cycads, can be considered a risk factor in the pathogenesis of ALS-PDC and idiopathic PD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BMAA, the toxin responsible for ALS-PDC, is a mixed glutamatergic receptor agonist, and the specific pathways activated on SNpc DAergic neurons are mGluR and TRP channels.
BMAA is not only toxic to the motor neurons in ALS-PDC but also to the SNpc DAergic neurons.
BMAA is toxic to DA neurons and the mechanism of toxicity involves mGluR activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BMAA is an excitotoxic compound that can damage DAergic neurons in a mGluR-1 dependent manner.
mGluR-activated pathways are a major mechanism by which BMAA induces DAergic cell death in the SNpc.
the mGluRs and TRP channels are potential therapeutic targets for ALS-PDC and PD.
